data.additionalDetails:
VYNEX Hood — Additional Details

Privacy-First Data Infrastructure

VYNEX Hood is designed to create a new model for data ownership: users can contribute valuable data without exposing their raw personal information.

Instead of sending sensitive data to centralized servers, VYNEX focuses on encrypted, privacy-preserving computation so useful insights can be generated while keeping the underlying data protected.

Core Technology

TEE — Trusted Execution Environment
Sensitive computations can run inside isolated secure environments designed to prevent unauthorized access to raw data.

MPC — Multi-Party Computation
Enables multiple parties to contribute to computations without requiring each party to reveal its private inputs.

Differential Privacy
Adds mathematical privacy protection to datasets and outputs, helping reduce the risk of identifying individual contributors.

Data Contributors

Users remain at the center of the ecosystem.

Contributors can provide approved data through supported devices, applications, or integrations while maintaining control over participation and consent.

The goal is simple:

Contribute data → Protect your privacy → Generate useful insights → Earn rewards.

Confidential Data Marketplace

VYNEX Hood can connect data contributors with researchers, developers, AI builders, and other organizations that need high-quality data insights.

Instead of selling raw personal information, the network is designed around privacy-preserving queries and aggregated insights.

DePIN + Privacy

VYNEX Hood brings privacy infrastructure to the DePIN ecosystem.

As more devices and networks generate valuable real-world data, VYNEX aims to provide the confidential layer that allows this data to become useful without turning users' private information into an exposed commodity.

User Ownership

VYNEX is built around a simple principle:

Your data should create value for you — without requiring you to surrender your privacy.

Users should have meaningful control over participation, consent, and how their data contributes to the network.

Vision

VYNEX Hood is working toward a confidential data economy where individuals, devices, DePIN networks, and data consumers can interact without compromising sensitive information.

Private data. Secure computation. Shared value.

VYNEX Hood — building the privacy layer for the next generation of DePIN.

data.name: Gladius protocol by Virtuals
data.description: Gladius Protocol builds baskets that never rebalance: 2 to 15 tokens locked into a single ERC-20 whose weights are written once and cannot be changed by anyone, including us. This is a community token. It carries no claim on the protocol, no share of revenue and no governance rights, because the contracts have nothing to govern and no revenue to divide. The protocol itself does not use it. The contracts, their tests and the documentation are public and meant to be checked.
data.tokenUtility:
None, and that is settled rather than pending.

The protocol has no parameters a vote could set, no treasury a token could direct and no fee stream a holder could receive. Basket compositions cannot be changed by any vote, the factory holds no power over what it deploys, and the router holds no funds between transactions. A token sold as a claim on any of those would be describing a different protocol.

Baskets mint and redeem in their own constituents and settle in USDG. That was true before this token and is true after it.

No one should expect to make money from holding it.
data.roadmap:
Nothing is deployed on any network yet.

In order: finish the deployment script for the router, deploy the factory to Robinhood Chain, then get the contracts audited. Minting goes live after that, not before it.

Known gaps are listed in the contracts README rather than left out. The router has only been exercised against pools without hooks, and there is no audit. Those two matter most and neither is finished.

This token is not a prerequisite for any of the above.
data.additionalDetails:
The contracts are unaudited and nothing is live on any network. No one should put money into them until an audit has happened. That sits at the top of the repository README rather than buried at the bottom.

Everything is open source. The site reads Robinhood Chain at request time with no database in between, and ships no web3 library at all: the ABI decoding is written by hand and tested against return data produced by the real contracts inside an EVM, because a decoding bug would not look like an error. It would look like a basket holding something it does not hold.
